symbols.x: an input: the feature values for one example (a single number when there is only one feature)
symbols.y: the true target value to predict; the tutorial also writes the whole list of targets as plain y
symbols.bf:y: the list of all true target values, one per training example
symbols.hat:y: the model's predicted value for an example
symbols.bar:x: the sample mean of x: the average of the x values
symbols.bar:y: the sample mean of y: the average of the y values
symbols.bar:X: the sample mean: the average of the sampled values
symbols.theta: a parameter the model learns: the weight on one feature (theta 0 is the intercept)
symbols.hat:theta: the fitted parameter values the method ends up with
symbols.w: the tutorial's name for the model's weights (w0 intercept, w1 slope)
symbols.hat:w: the fitted weights found by least squares (tutorial notation)
symbols.beta: the lab's name for the model's parameters (the same role as theta)
symbols.lambda: the penalty strength: how much large weights are charged; zero gives plain least squares
symbols.alpha: the learning rate: how big a step gradient descent takes; sklearn's alpha is penalty strength
symbols.X: the design matrix: one row per example, one column per feature, first column all ones
symbols.T: transpose: flips a vector or matrix so rows become columns
symbols.i: counts features (0 to n) in the model; in statistics and tutorial formulas it counts data points
symbols.n: the number of features, not counting the intercept (slide notation)
symbols.m: the number of training examples (the slides once also use m for a sample mean)
symbols.N: the number of values in a sample; written N(mean, variance) it is the normal distribution
symbols.p: the number of features (the tutorial counts the bias column, the lab does not)
symbols.k: the number of nearest neighbours in k-NN; inside the distance formula it counts features
symbols.K: the number of new features produced by a feature map
symbols.t: counts gradient descent steps: the parameter value after t steps
symbols.J: the cost: the total squared error of a candidate set of parameters
symbols.L: the tutorial's name for the loss: the average squared error
symbols.h: the prediction function: takes an input, returns the predicted value using the parameters
symbols.f: the true underlying function; in k-NN, the target value stored for a training point
symbols.hat:f: the model's learned estimate of the true function
symbols.E: the expected value: the average over many repeats
symbols.P: the probability (density) of what is written before the bar, given what follows
symbols.cal:L: the likelihood: how probable the observed data is for a candidate parameter value
symbols.varepsilon: random noise: the part of y the line cannot explain
symbols.sigma: the standard deviation of the noise (its square is the variance)
symbols.mu: the population mean: the average over the whole population
symbols.b: the lab's name for a parameter (b0 intercept, b1 slope); in Laplace noise, the noise scale
symbols.r: the Pearson correlation: a unit-free number from -1 to +1 for linear association
symbols.s: the sample standard deviation (s squared is the sample variance)
symbols.F: the unknown distribution the samples are drawn from
symbols.S: a sum of products of deviations from the mean (S_xx for x, S_xy for x and y)
symbols.R: the R squared score: how much of the variation in y the model explains
symbols.D: an indicator variable: 1 if the patient takes the drug, 0 if not
symbols.z: the interaction feature: the drug indicator multiplied by age
symbols.u: any vector, used as a stand-in input; in the derivative hints, the variable being differentiated
symbols.v: an arbitrary vector in the derivative hint
symbols.A: an arbitrary matrix in the derivative hint
symbols.g: an example function whose lowest value is used to compare min and arg min
symbols.I: the identity matrix: ones on the diagonal, zeros elsewhere; adding lambda I adds lambda to the diagonal
symbols.Phi: the design matrix of the new features, one row per example, one column per new feature
symbols.phi: the feature map: turns an input into a new list of features
symbols.bb:R: the set of real numbers (R to the p is lists of p real numbers)
symbols.Delta: a change in the value that follows
symbols.q: labels the query point: the new input we want a prediction for
symbols.sum: add up the term that follows, once for every value of the index shown
symbols.min: the smallest value the expression that follows can take
symbols.arg: the input value that gives the best score, rather than the score itself (read with min)
symbols.partial: the slope of the cost with respect to one parameter, nudging only that one
symbols.norm: the length of a vector; squared, it is the sum of its squared entries
symbols.abs: the size of the number inside, ignoring its sign
symbols.mid: given: what comes after the bar is known or fixed
symbols.sim: is drawn from, or is distributed as
symbols.propto: is proportional to: equal up to a fixed constant factor
symbols.exp: e raised to the power of the term that follows
symbols.log: the natural logarithm of the term that follows
symbols.w:var: the variance: the average squared spread around the mean
symbols.w:cov: the covariance: how much two variables move together
symbols.w:rmse: root mean squared error: a typical prediction miss, in the units of y
symbols.w:mae: mean absolute error: the average size of the miss, ignoring sign
symbols.w:adjusted: labels the version of R squared adjusted for the number of features
symbols.w:mse: mean squared error: the average squared prediction miss
symbols.w:bias: how far the model's average prediction is from the true value
symbols.w:variance: how much the model's prediction changes from one training set to another
symbols.w:irreducible error: the noise error that no model can remove
symbols.w:diag: a matrix with the listed numbers down the diagonal and zeros elsewhere
symbols.w:age: the patient's age, used as a feature

The big picture.beta: the lab's name for the model's parameters (theta in the slides, w in the tutorial)
The big picture.alpha: the lab's penalty strength (sklearn's alpha), the same role as lambda
The big picture.p: the number of features in the tutorial (it includes the bias column) and the lab (it does not)

Gradient descent.J: the cost being reduced: squared error of the current parameters (one example, or summed over all)
Gradient descent.j: counts training examples; x_ji is feature i of example j

Probabilistic interpretation.N: the normal (Gaussian) distribution, written with its mean and variance
Probabilistic interpretation.b: the scale of Laplace noise: larger b means wider noise
Probabilistic interpretation.sigma: the standard deviation of the Gaussian noise

Statistics background.n: the number of values in the sample
Statistics background.i: counts the values in the sample
Statistics background.X: one random value drawn from the population
Statistics background.theta: an unknown population parameter we want to estimate from the sample
Statistics background.p: the probability of heads on a bent coin: an example of a population parameter
Statistics background.sigma: the population standard deviation (Greek letters are for populations, not samples)

Univariate linear regression.w: the tutorial's weights: w0 is the intercept and w1 the slope

Multiple linear regression.w: a person's weight, the quantity predicted from height and body frame
Multiple linear regression.hat:w: the predicted body weight of a person
Multiple linear regression.h: a person's height, one of the inputs
Multiple linear regression.b: a person's body frame, one of the inputs

Linear regression for curve shapes.n: the number of data points (tutorial notation)
Linear regression for curve shapes.p: the number of original input features before the feature map
Linear regression for curve shapes.w: the weights on the new features
Linear regression for curve shapes.hat:w: the fitted weights on the new features

Regularisation.i: counts the features being penalised; the slides' first penalty sum starts at 1, skipping the intercept
Regularisation.lambda: the penalty strength; the sources disagree on whether the intercept is also charged
Regularisation.norm: the length of the weight vector; squared, the sum of squared weights (may include the intercept)
Regularisation.I: the identity matrix; lambda I adds lambda to every diagonal entry, intercept's included (sklearn skips it)
Regularisation.X: the design matrix (one row per example); in the lab results, X_3 and X_4 are named feature columns
Regularisation.n: the number of features in the penalty sum; in the lab data, 38 is the sample count

Local (nearest.i: labels one training point; in the average it counts the k neighbours
Local (nearest.j: the second of the two points whose distance is measured
Local (nearest.f: the target value stored for a training point
Local (nearest.n: the number of features; in x_n it names the nearest training point to the query
Local (nearest.k: the number of nearest neighbours; inside the distance sum, a feature index

Bias-variance.f: the true underlying function that generates the targets
Bias-variance.E: the expected value over many possible training sets and noise

Model evaluation.R: the R squared score: 1 for perfect, 0 for matching the mean-only guess
Model evaluation.m: the number of samples (adjusted R squared uses m-1 and m-n-1)

Worked examples.n: the number of data points (tutorial notation)
Worked examples.w: the tutorial's weights: w0 is the intercept and w1 the slope
Worked examples.p: the number of columns of X, including the column of ones

Exam traps.theta: a parameter of the model (in theta1 x over theta2 plus x, not a plain weight)

Errors and inconsistencies.n: the number of samples in the tutorial and lab; the number of features in the slides
Errors and inconsistencies.h: the prediction function; in the p.67 typo, a person's height
Errors and inconsistencies.w: the tutorial's weights; in the p.67 typo, a person's body weight
Errors and inconsistencies.alpha: sklearn's name for the penalty strength (like lambda); elsewhere the learning rate
Errors and inconsistencies.z: the interaction feature D times Age; in the Q2(a) hint, it is mixed up with the vector u
